summary: Promote the browser-submit gate out of per-ticket throwaways into `make browser`
description:
Shipped as `a9b81de` (2026-08-06) and **never created on the board** — the key was used in a
commit without a ticket file ever existing. Reconstructed 2026-08-08 during a board validation.

Makes the one quality gate this repo cannot automate into a command anyone can run:
`make browser`, backed by `scripts/browser.sh`, with specs committed under `test/browser/`
rather than written from scratch per ticket and thrown away.

**This is the substance of TKT-196**, which was still sitting in Backlog when this landed under a
different key. See the disposition comment on TKT-196.

**Why it could not be part of `make check`:** it needs the host's real Chrome, so CI cannot run it.
That is a property of the gate, not a gap in it — `AGENTS.md` now says so explicitly.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Created retroactively on 2026-08-08. The work was already on `main`; this ticket exists so the board's history is not missing a key that its own commits reference.

<!-- sdlc:stage=building kind=summary -->
### Implementation — `a9b81de` (2026-08-06)

`+545 / −79` across 13 files.

- **`make browser`** → `scripts/browser.sh` (98 lines), with `scripts/stack-env.sh` (68 lines)
  factored out so the browser gate and `scripts/smoke.sh` share one stack-environment derivation
  instead of duplicating it — `smoke.sh` shrank by 56 lines in the process.
- **`test/browser/reset-password.mjs`** (234 lines) — the first committed spec, submitting a real
  write path rather than only rendering it.
- **`AGENTS.md`** rewritten: the standing claim *"There is no Playwright/e2e harness in-repo yet"*
  is gone, replaced by the working agreement that a web-UI ticket which adds or changes a write
  form runs `make browser` and adds a spec.
- **A new learning**, `a-failed-optional-dependency-is-skipped-silently.md` (58 lines), plus an
  update to the existing browser-submit learning and `docs/development.md`.

**It immediately earned its keep:** TKT-226 used it to catch a `no-referrer` policy that nulled the
`Origin` header and 403'd every password reset, and TKT-224 used it to catch an undeclared 429 being
rewritten to 500 by the response validator — a defect no handler test could see, because handler
tests never cross the contract middleware.
